spa.eraLabel: 1995 · Towns OS V2.1 L51 — FM TOWNS (1989)

museum.arch: Intel 80386/486-class (FM TOWNS II), 4-6 MB, Towns sprite/CD-ROM chipset
museum.periodBrowser: none — Towns OS V2.1 L51 ships no TCP/IP stack by default
museum.blurb: Fujitsu shipped a CD-ROM drive as standard in a consumer PC in 1989, years early. Towns OS is its icon-first Japanese desktop on DOS — sprites, 16.7M-colour modes, Red Book soundtracks, sold in one country.
museum.notes: Host-native station: MAME's fmtowns-family driver runs on the host (drawshm frames, ctlsock keys, FIFO audio), no QEMU and no installed guest disk — the Towns System Software V2.1 L51 CD is the boot volume (-cdrom, a CHD composed by scripts/build-guests/tiles/fmtowns.sh from the bin/cue). Towns mouse on the second pad port (-pad2 mouse). See docs/lab/FMTOWNS-WAVE.md.

reset.mouse: PROVEN 2026-09-13 absolute, write route (docs/lab/FMTOWNS-WAVE.md SS Pointer, "Pointer stream 2026-09-13 #5"): Towns OS keeps the guest cursor position in THREE mirrored 16-bit little-endian words 2 bytes apart (order=hv) -- 0x11623c is the AUTHORITATIVE position (poke it and the driver propagates it and repaints), 0x0a2034 is a copy the driver overwrites on the next poll, and 0x116240 is the ERASE position the next poll restores before drawing -- writing anything but 0x11623c alone leaves a trail of stale arrows on screen. Towns OS only redraws on a NON-ZERO poll delta, so the module writes the position pre-biased by a 1-count nudge and then issues that one count (MAME_CTL_ABS_RAM=cpu=maincpu,pts=0x11623c,order=hv,nudge=1); no MAME_CTL_GAIN_X/Y -- must never be set on this station, the acceleration curve this route bypasses. The 640x480 Towns raster is letterboxed 931x702+61+48 on the published surface (MAME_CTL_ABS_RECT=61,48,931,702, MAME_CTL_ABS_GEOM=640x480). Five targets (80,70) (960,70) (80,720) (960,720) (512,384), TWO laps, arrow re-parked between every reading: the guest's own cursor word is EXACT on all ten (0 residual); worst locator error 3 px on (80,70) in both laps identically, which is the TownsMENU bar hiding the arrow tip, not pointer error. Click/drag/window-activation proven separately in "Pointer stream 2026-09-13 #2" (see reset.fixture / docs/lab/FMTOWNS-WAVE.md); a plain click on a desktop icon draws nothing by TownsMENU's own design.
reset.keyboard: PROVEN — real ctlsock KEY path through the generated fmtowns.keymap (79/146 fields matched); Ctrl+Esc opens the guest's own Task List dialog, pressed again opens a different dialog, proving live input (docs/lab/FMTOWNS-WAVE.md Proofs)
